A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETTA study. All 27 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including appendices A–G, provide readable text, tables, equations and figures supporting comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original audio-generation experiments, controlled ablations, human listening evaluations and VAE reconstruction results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports synthetic-caption quality ratings and training-loss comparisons.

M1.justification: The AF-Synthetic construction procedure, ETTA-VAE, ETTA-DiT components, training objectives and sampling procedures remain unchanged. The added analyses support existing design choices rather than introduce a new model component.

E1.justification: Training sources, AudioCaps/MusicCaps/SongDescriber evaluations, creative prompts and reconstruction datasets are retained. The new caption-quality study samples existing AudioSet, FreeSound/Laion-630k and WavCaps material without introducing a new domain or task requirement.

E2.justification: The new caption-quality comparison evaluates AF-Synthetic against Laion-630k captions, original FreeSound captions and WavCaps metadata-based captions (v2 Appendix C.2, Table 9). Generative-model and vocoder comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 removes VGGish-based FD_V from the evaluation suite while retaining the other objective metrics. The new caption-quality study randomly samples 100 audio-caption pairs from each of three existing subsets for five-point relevance ratings. Existing generation training budgets and sampling settings remain stable.

E4.justification: v2 adds human validation of synthetic-caption quality and Figure 4's controlled training-loss comparisons across architecture, objective and dataset choices. These provide additional evidence about caption fidelity and training stability. Existing architectural, scaling, sampling and negative-result analyses are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: The merged benchmark tables retain the earlier numerical uncertainty intervals but omit the explicit 95% confidence-interval labels previously supplied in v1 Tables 3, 5 and 23. The creative-audio Wilcoxon test remains unchanged; the new caption table uses the existing 95% interval reporting convention.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark scores remain unchanged, but FD_V results disappear. v2 adds ground-truth IS/CLAP scores, training-loss curves, caption-quality ratings and MusicCaps ETTA-FT-AC-100k listening scores of 3.30 ± 0.10 OVL and 3.44 ± 0.12 REL. Table 9 reports baseline-to-AF-Synthetic REL changes of 3.82 to 4.04, 3.68 to 3.83 and 3.92 to 4.02 across its three subsets. Table 6 also introduces a 2.34B parameter-count inconsistency with the retained 2.35B in Appendix Table 17.

T1.justification: Appendix B's assumptions, VAE losses, diffusion and flow-matching expressions, latent-distribution formulation and guidance equations retain their mathematical substance. Equation numbering and line wrapping change, without new proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about AF-Synthetic, systematic design-space investigation, ETTA's competitive generation quality and creative-caption following. New evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit training-divergence interpretations, frames the 1.44B choice as a size-quality balance and includes distortion as another explanation for high-CFG degradation. Conversely, it removes the FD_V shortfall discussion and specific caveats about unaugmented-data diversity and disagreement between metric-optimal CFG and human preferences.

D1.justification: v2 adds an ETTA code-repository link and identifies Mechanical Turk as the listening-evaluation platform. Appendix C.1 revises the CLAP checkpoint identifier from 630k-best to 630k-audioset-fusion-best, without establishing that data generation was rerun. The explicit CFG=3 disclosure for the RoPE/dropout ablations is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 removes the assertions that AutoCap is not open-sourced and positions AF-Synthetic more explicitly as scaling closely related captioning approaches. Kilgour et al.'s FAD reference is removed alongside FD_V; the broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Targeted edits condense results discussion and future work, revise appendix headings, add an Impact Statement and introduce caption-quality and training-loss explanations.

P2.justification: The document adopts a two-column conference layout throughout. Objective and subjective benchmark tables are merged, main-text ablations become compact summaries with fuller tables in the appendices, and new caption-quality and loss displays are added. Sampler figures are redesigned around FD_P instead of FD_V.

improvement.justification: Human caption ratings and controlled loss curves strengthen the evidence for existing dataset-quality and training-stability claims, while the repository link improves documented code access. These are limited gains: the core method and shared benchmark scores remain stable, and removing FD_V results, confidence-level labels and specific caveats reduces some reporting completeness.
